observed_ui_rules.statement: A refund can only be requested once per order; after a refund request is created, the "Request refund" action becomes unavailable and refund.status moves from none to pending.

inference.text: The workflow intends a refund to be requestable only once per order; the server should reject a second /api/order/refund/request call while a refund is already pending or completed.

observed_ui_rules.statement: The "Complete refund" action is available only while a refund is pending, and disappears permanently once the refund is completed (terminal, one-time completion).

inference.text: The workflow intends refund completion to occur exactly once; the server should reject a repeat /api/order/refund/complete call, and should reject the call entirely if no refund was ever requested (skip-step).

observed_ui_rules.statement: Price protection adjustment is presented as unavailable while another order request (a refund) is active.

facts.text: paragraph : Price protection is not available while another order request is active.

inference.text: The workflow intends price-protection adjustments and refund requests to be mutually exclusive per order; no price-adjustment endpoint was recorded in this session to test server-side enforcement directly.

conflicting_action_pairs_note: At step 1, "Request refund", "Cancel order", and "Request price adjustment" are co-visible state-changing controls. Only "Request refund" maps to a documented endpoint (POST /api/order/refund/request); "Cancel order" and "Request price adjustment" have no recorded HTTP request and no matching entry in endpoint_catalog.json. Per the endpoint-evidence contract, no URL may be fabricated for them, so no actionable conflicting_action_pairs entry can be formed. See unresolved_ui_affordances below.

critical_endpoints.why: Creates a pending refund of the full order amount ($100). Financial state transition; drives refund.status none->pending and gates the subsequent completion step. Agent inference (unverified): the endpoint takes no request body and may not validate order state server-side before creating a duplicate/second refund request while one is already pending or after completion.

Marks the refund completed and sets totalReturned=100 / netCustomerBenefit=0 — this is the actual money-movement step. Agent inference (unverified): calling this endpoint directly without a prior refund/request (skip-step), or calling it twice in a row / concurrently (replay / double-spend), may allow totalReturned to exceed originalAmount (100), which would be a direct financial-loss bug.
